source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 6: systematics and evolutionary relationships; taxonomic categories and hierarchy; taxon; common categories and lowest category; characters used in classification; and the definition and examples of species.

questions.question: Which title of publication is mentioned on this page in connection with Linnaeus?
questions.explanation: The page says Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication.
questions.source_text: used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication

questions.question: According to the page, which areas were later included in the enlarged scope of systematics?
questions.explanation: The page states that systematics later expanded to include identification, nomenclature and classification.
questions.source_text: The scope of systematics was later enlarged to include identification, nomenclature and classification.

questions.question: Which relationship does systematics take into account according to the page?
questions.explanation: The page explicitly says systematics considers evolutionary relationships between organisms.
questions.source_text: Systematics takes into account evolutionary relationships between organisms.

questions.question: According to the page, classification is:
options: A hierarchy of steps, not a single-step process
A method based only on habitat
questions.explanation: The text explains that classification involves a hierarchy of steps.
questions.source_text: Classification is not a single step process but involves hierarchy of steps

questions.question: What does each step in the classification hierarchy represent?
questions.explanation: Each step represents a rank or category.
questions.source_text: each step represents a rank or category

questions.question: Why is a category called a taxonomic category in the passage?
options: It is part of the overall taxonomic arrangement
It is always the lowest level
questions.explanation: The page links the term taxonomic category to its place in the overall taxonomic arrangement.
questions.source_text: Since the category is a part of overall taxonomic arrangement, it is called the taxonomic category

questions.question: What do all taxonomic categories together constitute?
questions.explanation: The page says all categories together constitute the taxonomic hierarchy.
questions.source_text: all categories together constitute the taxonomic hierarchy

questions.question: A category, as a unit of classification, is commonly termed a:
questions.explanation: The passage says a category is commonly termed a taxon, plural taxa.
questions.source_text: Each category, referred to as a unit of classification, in fact, represents a rank and is commonly termed as taxon (pl.: taxa).

questions.question: Which shared feature of insects is given as an example on the page?
options: Two pairs of wings in every insect
questions.explanation: The page uses three pairs of jointed legs as a common feature of insects.
questions.source_text: Insects represent a group of organisms sharing common features like three pairs of jointed legs.

questions.question: In the page's explanation, what does a category further denote?
questions.explanation: The page directly states that category denotes rank.
questions.source_text: Category further denotes rank.

questions.question: How are taxonomic groups or categories described on this page?
options: Distinct biological entities, not merely morphological aggregates
Only groups of organisms with identical appearance
Only names used in local languages
questions.explanation: The page distinguishes taxonomic groups as biological entities rather than mere morphological aggregates.
questions.source_text: These taxonomic groups/categories are distinct biological entities and not merely morphological aggregates.

questions.question: Which common categories are listed on the page?
questions.explanation: The page lists kingdom, phylum or division for plants, class, order, family, genus and species.
questions.source_text: kingdom, phylum or division (for plants), class, order, family, genus and species

questions.question: What does the page identify as the lowest category in both plant and animal kingdoms?
questions.explanation: The text says all organisms, including plants and animals, have species as the lowest category.
questions.source_text: All organisms, including those in the plant and animal kingdoms have species as the lowest category.

questions.question: What is the basic requirement for placing an organism in various categories?
options: Knowledge of the characters of an individual or group of organisms
Knowing only the organism's local name
questions.explanation: The page identifies knowledge of organism characters as the basic requirement.
questions.source_text: The basic requirement is the knowledge of characters of an individual or group of organisms.

questions.question: Knowledge of organism characters helps identify what, according to the page?
questions.explanation: The text says characters help identify similarities and differences within the same kind and among different kinds of organisms.
questions.source_text: This helps in identifying similarities and dissimilarities among the individuals of the same kind of organisms as well as of other kinds of organisms.

questions.question: A group of individual organisms with what feature is considered a species in this passage?
questions.explanation: The page describes a species as a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
questions.source_text: Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species.

questions.question: According to the page, closely related species should be distinguished based on:
questions.explanation: The page says closely related species can be distinguished by distinct morphological differences.
questions.source_text: One should be able to distinguish one species from the other closely related species based on the distinct morphological differences.

questions.question: Which scientific names are used as examples in the species section on this page?
questions.explanation: The page gives mango, potato and lion as Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum and Panthera leo.
questions.source_text: Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion).

questions.question: In Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum and Panthera leo, which set contains the specific epithets identified on the page?
questions.explanation: The page explicitly identifies indica, tuberosum and leo as specific epithets.
questions.source_text: All the three names, indica, tuberosum and leo, represent the specific epithets

questions.question: Which words are identified as genera in the examples Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum and Panthera leo?
questions.explanation: The first words in these scientific names—Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera—are identified as genera.
questions.source_text: while the first words Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are genera
